predeclaration.pass_criterion_summary: (a) 5 of 5 target_reached; (b) every landing <= 0.15 m; (c) no run uses all 3 mid-drive realignments; (d) zero safety-gate trips, zero containment breaches, stop confirmed every run.

build.card_note: Predeclaration trap 1: the card auto-splits above SPLIT_LEG_TARGET_METRES (3.85 m) and would have measured the splitter. The service was dispatched directly.

verdict.determination: The predeclared criterion is 5 of 5. One confirmed FAIL (run 2) was in hand at n=4, so the best attainable outcome for a 5th dispatch was 4 of 5 -- which predeclaration section 6 names explicitly as a FAIL with an informative failure, not a partial success. No 5th run could have produced a PASS.
verdict.abort_reason: Five consecutive attempts to establish a safe start position/heading for run 5 failed, ending in loss of daylight (vio_tracked_features 80 -> 0, current_orientation reason vio_feed_degraded) on top of an unstable BLE link. Reported as an aborted series per predeclaration section 7: partial n is a result, not a draft.
verdict.rate_note: DO NOT quote 3/4 or 75% as a reliability rate. n=4 against a targeted n=5, in an aborted series, with the start-geometry precondition violated (see heading_model_check). These are per-item records. Predeclaration section 4 already states that even a clean n=5 is a SCREEN, not a certification.

a_all_five_target_reached.required: 5 of 5 dispatched runs return stop_reason target_reached

c_correction_budget_retains_margin.note: The budget is SHARED between the pre-linear post-turn alignment correction and the mid-drive re-aims -- realignments_used is incremented at both sites. Counting only mid-drive corrections would understate usage.

d_safety.required: zero safety-gate trips, zero containment breaches, stop confirmed on every run
d_safety.note: Also true of the five aborted run-5 attempts: nothing was dispatched in any refused direction, and the two live-gate refusals in step 5 of the incident sequence (ble_client_not_connected) are the gate working, not a trip against a scored run.

start_geometry_precondition.required: predeclaration section 3: the segment begins ALIGNED, single segment, no junction turn, so results are comparable to the banked 4/5/6 m reach runs
start_geometry_precondition.observed: NOT MET on any run. Targets were placed along toward + calibrated_forward_heading_offset_degrees (102.4). The executor's own VIO calibration drive measured the true forward direction 26.4 / 26.9 / 121.8 / 134.6 deg away from that, and runs 3 and 4 opened with STAGED turns of 122.88 and 135.553 deg. `toward` physically moved -20.9 / +22.8 / +120.7 / -138.1 deg across the opening turns, so the rotation was real.
start_geometry_precondition.consequence: Runs 3 and 4 are post-turn legs, which predeclaration section 3 puts explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this series. They are not comparable to the 0.1023 m banked 4.0 m prior. This alone would have voided the series independently of run 2.

profile_verification_summary.note: Verified key-by-key against each REAL run's echoed response, not only against the pre-dispatch dry run. Predeclaration section 3: a run whose echoed profile differs on any key is discarded, not scored. None had to be discarded on this ground.

landing_distribution.note: Reported as a distribution, per predeclaration section 4, NOT as a rate. n=4 in an aborted series with a violated start-geometry precondition; runs 3 and 4 are post-turn legs. Do not pool these with the banked aligned 4/5/6 m reach runs.

heading_model_check.question: Which model converts the mower's reported `toward` field into the map-frame direction it actually drives when told to go forward?

models.additive_offset: map_facing = toward + calibrated_forward_heading_offset_degrees (102.4 on the accepted profile). This is what heading_calibration.formula echoes and what the orchestrating session used to place every target tonight.
models.compass_mirror: map_facing = 90.13 - toward, the reflection implemented as _continuous_course_heading / _TOWARD_MIRROR_DEGREES and already used by the night turn path and by _current_orientation.

heading_model_check.method: For every linear pulse, compare the movement vector the executor itself measured (progress_diagnostics.movement_vector_heading_degrees, atan2(dy, dx) over the settled displacement) against each model evaluated on the `toward` reading live at the START of that pulse. Pulses are split by whether `toward` changed across the pulse, because every such pulse immediately follows a rotation and carries a stale reading.

toward_stale_post_rotation.note: Every one of these pulses is the first pulse of a run or the pulse immediately after a realignment turn. `toward` lags a rotation by one full pulse cycle (~5 s at the observed send gaps), which is the documented 'only valid when `toward` is fresh' caveat, now quantified.

heading_model_check.conclusion: On 30 real-hardware pulses with a fresh `toward`, the compass mirror predicts the driven direction to a mean absolute error of 1.000 deg (median 0.944, max 3.003). The additive offset is wrong by a mean of 87.478 deg (median 118.436, max 166.825). This is a measurement, not a proposed change.
heading_model_check.scope_limit: The additive offset did NOT steer these runs. In turn_mode 'vio' the executor closes on target_vision_heading derived from its own calibration drive; target_reported_heading_degrees is echoed but only steers the 'legacy' and 'night' turn paths. The damage was done upstream, where the orchestrating session used the offset to choose WHERE to put the target.
heading_model_check.authorizes: Nothing. Predeclaration section 10: a FAIL authorizes nothing beyond writing up the failure mode. Any change to calibrated_forward_heading_offset_degrees or to the accepted profile needs its own predeclaration and its own Gate 5.

post_series_incident_sequence.title: Map/corridor near-miss, caught before dispatch
post_series_incident_sequence.severity: caught by the pre-dispatch map scan
post_series_incident_sequence.detail: The first candidate start for run 5 put the polygon boundary -- near what proved to be the dock's own exclusion notch -- within 0.29 m of the 4.0 m corridor plus its 1.0 m overshoot margin. Nothing was dispatched. A 'turn right 30 deg' alternative was scanned and found WORSE: it exits the mapped area partway through. Also not dispatched.

post_series_incident_sequence.title: Confirmed map inaccuracy, caught by physical measurement, not software
post_series_incident_sequence.severity: hazard invisible to both software checks
post_series_incident_sequence.detail: At a later candidate the map-based corridor scan showed 3.5 m of clearance in the computed direction. The operator measured the actual distance to a real fence in that same direction at 110 inches = 2.79 m -- 0.71 m less than the map, and less than the 4.0 m segment itself needs. Nothing was dispatched.
post_series_incident_sequence.key_point: The software containment gate would have shown ample margin, and so would the map-polygon corridor scan that CLAUDE.md prescribes as the gate's backstop. A physical operator measurement caught a real hazard that both software checks would have missed. The map polygon is not ground truth.

post_series_incident_sequence.title: THE INCIDENT: a real dispatch in an unintended direction, from trusting heading telemetry immediately after a manual reposition
post_series_incident_sequence.severity: real hardware moved in a direction nobody intended
post_series_incident_sequence.detail: The operator repositioned/turned the mower by hand. With no intervening real motion, the orchestrating session computed a 0.5 m 'test' move from the then-current `toward` of 91.8054 deg using target_map_heading = toward + 102.4, giving a commanded map bearing of 194.205 deg. The move dispatched, returned stop_reason target_reached, and looked successful in telemetry. The operator reported directly and unambiguously that the mower had driven in the direction it was facing BEFORE the manual reposition.
post_series_incident_sequence.vio_heading_source: report_data.vision_info.heading, surfaced as the `vio_heading` sensor description in custom_components/mammotion/sensor.py

current_orientation_after_move.note: Reproduces exactly from the quoted post-move raw values: mirror 90.13 - (-101.8713) = 192.001, VIO (-168.570) % 360 = 191.430, gap 0.571 deg.

post_series_incident_sequence.UNRESOLVED_ARITHMETIC_DISCREPANCY: The quoted pre-move raw values do NOT reproduce a ~178 deg disagreement. mirror 90.13 - 91.8054 = 358.325 and VIO (-1.754) % 360 = 358.246 differ by 0.079 deg, which is well inside _ORIENTATION_AGREEMENT_TOLERANCE_DEGREES (15.0) and would have published trustworthy: true. Either the 178 deg figure was read at a different instant, or the two raw values were. This must be re-derived from the session transcript before anyone builds on either version -- and the second branch is the more alarming one: it would mean both independent heading sources were stale TOGETHER and corroborated each other at 0.079 deg while both described the pre-reposition facing.
post_series_incident_sequence.most_likely_mechanism: The device's own heading estimate -- both the compass-like `toward` field and VIO -- does not immediately reflect a manual physical reposition. It takes real subsequent motion to re-anchor what is plausibly a genuine ~180 deg-scale ambiguity after the machine is picked up and turned by hand. Both sources jumped ~166-167 deg on the first real motion after the reposition, and only then did they agree at 0.571 deg.
post_series_incident_sequence.classification: A telemetry-trust and process failure by the orchestrating session. NOT a control-law problem: the mower did what it was told with the input it was given.
post_series_incident_sequence.documented_risk_that_was_not_applied: The standing guidance is to re-derive facing two ways before every armed run -- the last driven leg's travel bearing and (90.13 - toward) with `toward` fresh -- and, on disagreement, to trust the mirror. It was skipped because a 0.5 m 'test' move made right after a manual reposition was treated as lower-stakes than an armed predeclared run. It was not.

post_series_incident_sequence.title: Second physical-measurement catch, immediately after the incident
post_series_incident_sequence.detail: The operator measured the actual fence distance in the new post-move facing at 1.83 m -- again well short of the 4.0 m the segment needs. A subsequent '180 deg turn' candidate was map-scanned and found to exit the mapped area at about 2.0 m of the needed 4.0 m, leaving 0.503 m of clearance. Neither was dispatched.

post_series_incident_sequence.title: BLE instability, then loss of daylight -- the system's own gates closed the door
post_series_incident_sequence.severity: session ended by conditions, not by a decision
post_series_incident_sequence.detail: A bounded turn-only diagnostic (raw_pymammotion_turn_to_heading, an in-place rotation, dry-run-verified clean beforehand) was refused twice by the live gate with ble_client_not_connected, corroborated by the binary_sensor ble_link_live reading off at -74 dBm -- at the documented failure threshold for this hardware (works above ~-70, dies below ~-76). On a third attempt BLE reported live (-66 dBm, ble_link_live on, real_motion_allowed true) and the command was accepted, but the HTTP call to Home Assistant timed out after 60 s. No active motion session was found immediately afterwards -- the device-side command sequence had completed, not hung -- but the very next telemetry read showed current_orientation.reason vio_feed_degraded, vio_feed_live false, and vio_tracked_features 0, down from 80 earlier in the session.
post_series_incident_sequence.interpretation: The tracked-feature collapse is this project's documented nightfall signature -- tracked_features is a cliff, not a gauge; 80 means saturated/enough light and it falls fast when light goes -- not a sensor glitch. Standing decision 4 (night is CLOSED) and the predeclaration's own 'daylight throughout' requirement both bind here.
post_series_incident_sequence.authorization_record: The orchestrating session had recommended stopping and stated the risk plainly (deteriorating conditions, the prior incident). The operator made the call to try one bounded, already-dry-run-verified, low-risk command anyway -- a turn-in-place, not a drive. No gate was overridden. The production system's own safety gates, first BLE and then implicitly the VIO/darkness condition discovered right after, are what actually stopped further motion.

session_close.note: Predeclaration section 8 and CLAUDE.md's motion-gate section: always verify a disarm from the live API AND RAW core.config_entries. HA writes .storage lazily, so a RAW read taken immediately after a disarm can lie for ~15 s.

what_this_authorizes: Nothing beyond this write-up. Predeclaration section 10. In particular: Phase 2 continuous steering (standing decision 5), accuracy (standing decision 3) and night (standing decision 4) are untouched, and no bound, tolerance or profile key is changed by anything here.
